This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #45681
* #45917
* #45462
* __->__ #45916
* #45915

## Motivation

GGUF MoE must discard padded and nonlocal routes without consuming their expert outputs or NaN scores. Preparing safe IDs and clearing intermediate tensors on every call adds allocations and launches, while an unguarded native projection can form a weight address from a negative ID.

This PR moves CUDA vector-route safety into a local native consumer, shares its format math with the AOT implementation, and preserves per-slot product rounding before the existing MoE reduction. It also restores lazy fallback accumulation and repairs the shared native MMQ bounds/scale indexing.

## Changes

- CUDA MMVQ uses a local JIT entry with negative-ID checks before expert-address formation. Ordinary contiguous int32 routes retain their storage; exceptional layouts/widths normalize explicitly. The quantize/project structure and zeroed projection output remain intact.
- CUDA weighting excludes inactive outputs and scores inside its product kernel, removing activation-sized input copies and separate intermediate clears. Products still round to the output dtype before native `moe_sum`.
- Shared native GGUF code checks MMQ slack bounds before access and indexes Q8_1 scales with the same routed row as the values. Rebuilt MUSA providers can use the native in-place weighting operator; older providers retain their compatibility path.
- The slow fallback adopts the first valid expert result, adds later contributions in order, and zeros the existing final row only when all routes are inactive.
- A local non-flushing FP32 multiply preserves subnormal operands/results and signed zero in CUDA weighting, including SM90 fast-math builds. MUSA multiplication and the reducer are unchanged.
- Shared GGUF headers have one AOT source owner, with JIT forwarding links. Source-distribution staging materializes those headers so the runtime package remains self-contained.

## Review order

1. `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/gguf.py`: vector/MMQ/fallback selection, private-buffer lifetimes and final weighting/reduction.
2. `kernels/ops/moe/gguf_moe_vec.py`, `jit/csrc/moe/gguf_moe_vec.cuh` and the shared GGUF headers: preserved format math and negative-ID access guards.
3. `aot/csrc/moe/moe_sum.cu`, `gguf_moe_weights.cuh` and the weighting wrappers: validation, rounding and device registration.
4. `test_gguf_inactive_routes.py`, `test_gguf_moe_weights.py`, then `python/setup.py` for standalone header packaging.

- Define unused CUDA MMQ expert-map capacity in the existing alignment producer. This removes the per-call arange, multiply, comparison and masked-fill sequence while retaining the released provider and buffer sizes.

## CI cadence

The GGUF all-format/AOT numerical regression and weighting/vector microbenchmark now run in `nightly-test-1-gpu-large`. The compact full-entry GGUF tests remain in base CI; the MUSA nightly registration is preserved.

Across the stack, six existing CUDA file registrations move from base CI to extra/nightly, removing 854 estimated GPU-seconds from the default gate (registration estimates, not a measured wall-time saving). All test bodies, cases, inputs, assertions and tolerances are unchanged. Full before/after discovery validates 2,535 files and 3,077 registrations, with every moved file selected in its enabled destination suite. Configured hooks pass; native tests were not rerun for this registration-only update.

## Validation

- Final integrated `e6670af1ad` B300 MMQ comparison against reviewed stack `5ece6073f3`: Q4_0/Q8_0, M65/512, FP16 H256/I256/E4/topk2. Balanced ABBA workers with 32 captured calls × 8 replays × 9 samples show lower GPU time in all four cases: hot graph 10.1–27.7% and cold-L2 graph 11.4–18.7% (256 MiB flush excluded by events). Valid outputs are bitwise identical. Each entry removes 4 GPU launches; allocated peak decreases by 512 bytes at M65 and 2560 bytes at M512. This is a comparison to the reviewed stack; earlier original-main controls below retain their separate baseline and limitations.
- A native Q8_0 identity projection exposed a reference-only Q8_1 rounding-tie error: scalar division had become reciprocal multiplication. The test reference now uses tensor division, with the same inputs and numerical tolerance. No production numerical kernel or math setting changed.

- At integrated `e6670af1ad`, the alignment suite passes 89 tests on 1× H200 and 1× B300, covering count publication, signed IDs, complete expert-map capacity and combined options during graph replay. The GGUF native-entry suite passes 7 tests on B300 with sglang-kernel 0.4.10. H200 uses PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 for the source-local JIT producer; this is not full native H200 GGUF admission.

Based on #45915 above main `25ad569ff9`. Blackwell checks ran on integrated source `f3a116529a`; the GGUF runtime, production weighting TU/header and registered kernel test match this PR's `b80e51a006` exactly.

On **1× NVIDIA B300, SM10.3**, with PyTorch **2.14.1+cu130**, Triton **3.8.0**, sgl-kernel **0.4.10**, FlashInfer **0.7.2** and NVCC **13.0.88**:

- The registered vector-format/Triton-weighting checks passed **2 tests / 45 subtests**. Vector coverage compares 19 formats against the existing native provider, with FP16/BF16/FP32 coverage for selected formats and inactive/recovery graph states.
- The exact production `moe_sum.cu` was separately compiled with the precise SM100-family `compute_100f/sm_100f` flags. Dedicated process-local registration passed **2 tests / 44 subtests**: native/Triton rounding cases plus native amplified-subnormal, subnormal-result and signed-zero cases, including poisoned inactive routes.
- All **18** generated weighting specializations contain `mul.rn.f32` without FTZ multiplication. Six graph captures passed **24** valid/partial/all-inactive/recovery replays with strided metadata. Ten invalid/overlap cases and three empty shapes passed; FP16 output `[8192, 4096]` required **0 extra allocated peak bytes** for the warmed native weighting call.
- The seven GGUF unit tests, including fallback operation budgets and borrowed input/ID preservation, passed within the combined CPU suite. Normal configured pre-commit hooks passed.

The dedicated weighting library does **not** establish full-provider or model compatibility: the installed provider was unchanged, and CUDA serving uses the local vector entry plus Triton weighting. Full rebuilt-wheel validation, native MUSA/MCC execution, distributed/model parity and GGUF serving performance remain untested. No universal performance claim follows from these operator checks; eager CPU submission overhead is excluded from the performance scope.

## Rebase validation (before the CI registration fix)

This five-PR stack was rebased without conflicts onto main `8b9f72417f`. All five patches retain their stable patch IDs relative to the preceding published stack; the newer main commits do not touch the stack's changed files. The existing removal of the unused `materialized_routing` parameter and its three call-site arguments in #45917 is preserved.

Each rebased PR commit passed its configured pre-commit checks independently. The final stack passes `git diff --check`, and all 72 changed Python files parse successfully. CPU test suites, native GPU tests and performance measurements were not rerun for this rebase. Previously reported results, including those at integrated `e6670af1ad`, remain evidence for those earlier revisions with their stated limits.

## Prior CI registration fix

The GGUF weighting test now uses the existing `nightly-musa-1-gpu` suite with `nightly=True`; at that revision, its CUDA kernel-unit registration was unchanged. The previous nonexistent MUSA suite caused global registry validation to fail before CPU, CUDA and AMD tests could run.

The original collection failure was reproduced. Full registration collection and suite validation now pass on the GGUF component (2,533 files / 3,075 registrations) and the integrated stack (2,535 files / 3,077 registrations), including enabled MUSA nightly and CUDA selection. Configured pre-commit checks pass for the corrected test. This update changes one registration line and is propagated through the existing stack.

## CPU CI follow-up

Run [39935811691](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39935811691) exposed an upstream Flux2 import test registered in the CPU suite, whose environment lacks the diffusion dependencies. The import chain also queries the active GPU. #45915 moves that check to the existing CUDA diffusion unit suite, which installs those dependencies, while retaining its XPU registration and the real subprocess check that blocks Intel Triton imports. This registration fix is propagated through the stack.

The Flux2 import check passes on 1× NVIDIA B300 with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0 and Diffusers 0.37.0; its five Intel-XPU numerical cases are skipped on CUDA and were not rerun on XPU. Full integrated registry collection validates 2,535 files / 3,077 registrations, including the enabled diffusion/XPU selections and the preceding GGUF MUSA fix. Configured checks pass for the changed files. Only three test files change across this follow-up; production code is unchanged. A fresh full CI result is not claimed.

## Merge preparation

Rebased this component onto main `1340044e97` for squash merge. The preceding stack components are already merged into main; only this component is replayed here. No test suites or performance measurements were rerun for this merge. Earlier validation sections describe their named revisions.
